Subject: Re: production deploy v21beta — spike in p95 tokens and some 504s

Sergio,

We pushed the v21beta variant to 60% traffic at 02:00 UTC last night (per the runbook). Immediately saw a 20% jump in p95 token latency and a handful of 504 timeouts across two critical routes (chat.complete and assistant.stream). Our frontend started returning degraded experiences for some power users around 02:15 UTC.

Attached a short CSV that captures the SLO hits measured by our side, plus a few sample traces and error messages. We need this flagged as an SLA-affecting incident; legal is copied because this impacts our ability to meet contractual latency commitments.

Request: can Redwood pin NimbleFin traffic back to the previous variant (v20stable) or authorize an emergency rollback? If rollback isn't possible immediately, we request a temporary SLA tolerance window until 08:00 UTC while we stabilize.

Tim
Lead Product, NimbleFin

Sergio / team — I pulled tenant-level telemetry and corroborate NimbleFin's p95 jump. Summary:
- Route: chat.complete and assistant.stream
- Observed p95 increase: from ~320ms to ~410ms (tokens) for the peak window; token service contribution appears to be +90ms on average
- Error rate: 504s increased from ~0.02% to 0.18% for the affected routes
- Canary region: US-West; the v21beta rollout impacted only this region for NimbleFin

I also attached a trimmed perf snapshot from the serving nodes for the 02:10 UTC period (v21beta_perf_snapshot.log) with a handful of stack traces showing elevated coroutine wait times in tokenization codepaths.

Short-term options: 1) pin NimbleFin traffic to v20stable at the routing layer (we can do this without a full rollback) — ETA 10 minutes after approval; 2) rollback cluster for the customer's routing group — ETA ~30 minutes but involves coordination with infra and may impact other customers on the same pool; 3) activate degraded-SLO tolerance (customer-facing concession) while we root-cause.

I recommend option 1 immediately to stop impact and buy time to investigate.

Ben
Sr. Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 03 May 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: production deploy v21beta — spike in p95 tokens and some 504s

Confirmed — SE telemetry looks like tokenization expansion in v21beta is creating slightly larger per-token latency under specific sequence shapes (longer system prompts + multi-turn). We're seeing increased KV-cache misses and an additional attention kernel fallback for sequences >2048 that were previously not exercised.

Operationally: we can do a traffic-pin for NimbleFin to v20stable at the router level (no customer restart) — Ben's ETA of ~10 minutes is accurate. A full rollback of v21beta cluster needs Eng lead approval if it would force re-deploy of shared infra; for a single-tenant pin it's low-risk.

Notes for customer communications and approval:
- If we pin to v20stable, throughput and latency should return to baseline within two token windows (~5–10 minutes) for existing in-flight requests.
- We'll reserve a mitigation hold window of 4 hours after pin to run targeted perf tests and gather root-cause evidence.
- If we need to revert globally later, we will follow the rollback runbook and pre-notify affected customers.

I will prepare a short tech brief with the root-cause indicators and evidence to support a temporary SLA concession if NimbleFin's legal requires it.

Kimberly
Lead, Serving Runtime Engineering
